sources.quote: Fisher Sand & Gravel at $9.54B is the civilian shock: a construction firm sitting next to Electric Boat and Lockheed because of DHS border barrier tasking.
sources.searcher_note: USAspending-based analysis of Jan-Jun 2026 contracts: DHS $40.5B (No. 2 agency), CBP $26.4B, Fisher $9.54B. Calendar H1, not FY Oct-Jun; no multi-year baseline.

sources.quote: the federal government has awarded his company over $9 billion to build even more border wall
sources.searcher_note: Fisher's firm got over $9B in wall awards; CBP gave nearly $14B (about 73% of contract value) to Fisher and Barnard; lawsuit over the awards.

sources.quote: Out of that tidal wave of money, Fisher Sand & Gravel Co. has landed more than $8 billion in contracts from the Department of Homeland Security and related agencies.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found coverage of Fisher's DHS contract total (>$8B), relaying the Bloomberg feature of the same day.

sources.quote: After spending roughly $2 billion a month on new border contracts in January and February, CBP more than doubled that pace in March alone.
sources.searcher_note: Monthly tracker of the CBP/DHS contract surge (over $7.5B on wall in March 2026). No comparison to a FY2019-25 median.

sources.quote: The project falls under a larger contract given to Fisher that includes numerous projects for border construction with a potential spending cap of $4.1 billion.

notes: Fisher's DHS contract haul is widely covered. Totals by source: >$8B (Bloomberg via Hoodline, Mar 2026), >$9B (ProPublica, May 2026), $9.54B for Jan-Jun 2026 (Fed-Spend), $13.4B across 18 awards (PrimeRFP, data as of Sep 2026). No source found that gives DHS's $50.97B Oct 2025-Jun 2026 total, the 4.1x-versus-FY2019-25-median comparison, or the $27.0B border-barrier figure.
